_readme: Q89 inc.11 — the 2026-06-16 pre-meeting discovery call with Alex of Gulf Coast RE Group, as an
Activity row the CRM can read. Fourth meeting through the same publisher, same gate, same two
surfaces, no new code.
WHY THIS ROW MATTERS MORE THAN ITS SIZE SUGGESTS: C-2018 already carries the 2026-07-22 Phase 1
KICKOFF (inc.7). This is the call five weeks EARLIER that produced it — the discovery. The
kickoff record shows what we agreed to build; this one shows why he agreed, in his own numbers
and his own words. A company record that holds the second meeting and not the first tells Rob
what was decided while hiding what was said.
PROVENANCE — read before trusting a line of it. Every item below was read out of the Notion
Master Meetings Database page `Gulf Coast Realty, AI Alex meeting one`
`find_meeting.py --page … --deep`, output archived in-repo at
`MLE Internal Meetings/archive-reads/2026-06-16-gulfcoast-ai-alex-one.deepread.txt` (47,171
bytes) and logged in `docs/research/Q84-READ-LOG-2026-08-05.md`. Nothing here was written from
memory, from a summary of a summary, or from another agent's prose.
THE SAME FOUR FIELDS LIE ON THIS ROW TOO — the sixth row in a row. Call Recording, Meeting
Summary, Google Doc Link and Export Status are all empty while the body holds 44,547 chars.
Field-emptiness is not evidence of absence anywhere in this system, and six consecutive
confirmations mean it is no longer a surprise to be re-flagged — it is a property of this
database.
`sourceRef` addresses the LINE, not the meeting. `body ¶NNN` is the 1-based index of the block
among ALL `[paragraph]` blocks of the deep export in file order (228 of them; 223 non-empty) —
the same convention as the Omega and Gulf Coast kickoff files. `body to_do N` and
`body bullet «heading»` address the summary blocks. No `url` is set on any item ON PURPOSE: the
Notion page URL opens a 44k-char MEETING, and a link that opens the meeting when the reader
expected the sentence is the lie `intelSource.ts` refuses to tell.
PAIN POINTS ARE THE CLIENT'S OWN WORDS. All four `text` values are literal substrings of their
`excerpt`, and all four excerpts are transcript paragraphs spoken by the Gulf Coast side about
their own operation — each is an ANSWER to a question Rob asked in the paragraph before it,
which is how the speaker is established on an unattributed Notion-AI transcript. Two further
candidates were REFUSED for exactly that reason: ¶202 ('with AI, you could spend six months
putting your heart and soul into something' and then a billionaire copies it) and ¶224 ('it gets
very frustrating', about dev shops reshuffling priorities) sit inside a two-way riff where the
speaker cannot be established from the text. Both are real concerns. Neither is provably the
CUSTOMER's, so neither is promoted into 'what the customer said'.
ACTION-ITEM STATUS IS NOT INFERRED. All four are written `open` because the page says nothing
about completion. Three of them are seven weeks old and the 2026-06-17 in-person meeting and the
2026-07-22 kickoff both happened, so some are very likely done — 'very likely' is not a status.
Marking them closed from a calendar inference is exactly the invented-field class this pipeline
exists to stop. A human closing them on the record is the correct way for them to close.
NOT WRITTEN HERE, DELIBERATELY. (a) The MLS scraping exchange (¶142–146: 'What if you're
grabbing all the data off of other websites that are using MLS?' … 'that's probably a little bit
of a gray area') is a hypothetical about working around a contract Gulf Coast has signed. It is
not an action item, nobody committed to it, and a company record Rob shows people is not where a
gray-area idea gets minuted. (b) No equity, split or money field is touched by this row — the
HomeCloneVault 35/65 that Rob corrected on 2026-07-27 is nowhere in this payload, and this
meeting predates it. (c) Origin Vault, Origin Stamp, Field Pulse, Boomtown, Bold Trail, Upwork
and Zillow are all named on the page and NONE of them became an org record: a vendor named in
passing is not a CRM org (inc.8/inc.10 precedent). Origin Vault is the one arguable case — it
has proposed a revenue-share partnership to Alex, not to Rob — so it is written as a talking
point about HIS deal, not as a company of ours.

Q89 inc.13 — RANKED. The four action items now carry `rank`, produced by `~/.claude/skills/meeting-next-steps/scripts/score_next_steps.py` from `data/meetings/2026-06-16-gulfcoast-ai-alex-one.nextsteps.json` against this same deep read, `--as-of 2026-08-05`. The rank is CARRIED, not computed here and not computed in the app: `meetingIntel` renders a block as ranked only when every item has one, so a partial ranking correctly falls back to source order. Ranks are byte-reproducible — the scorer reads no clock (as-of is a parameter) and ties break on item id. Nothing else on this row changed: no text was edited, no status was inferred, and the pain/talking/benefits blocks stay in source order because the scorer does not rank them.

intel.text: The Boomtown decision is already made and it is a two-year one: stay on legacy Boomtown for the ad-buying power, migrate nothing (agents rejected Bold Trail, and moving 60 of them is impractical), and build the replacement he owns outright. Pitching a migration is pitching against a decision.
intel.sourceRef: body bullet «Boomtown CRM: Pros, Cons & Migration Plans»
intel.excerpt: Boomtown launched Bold Trail as a successor, but agents who tested it returned negative feedback; migration of 60 agents is impractical — Plan: remain on legacy Boomtown for now, but build a proprietary replacement over the next ~2 years to fully own the platform

intel.text: On HomeCloneVault he already has money out the door and a partner circling: development funding is wired, the stack is Origin Vault + Origin Stamp + Field Pulse, and Origin Vault has asked him about a revenue-share partnership. That proposal is on HIS deal, not ours — worth knowing before anyone proposes terms near it.
intel.excerpt: Origin Vault. has asked me if I'll do some sort of a revenue share partnership. They see a lot of potential.

intel.text: His own read on why the site converts is conversion science, not design taste — Boomtown gets him ~10% visitor-to-lead where he says some sites run 5%. Any site we hand him will be judged against that number.
intel.excerpt: Purchasing power and the conversion rate, right? So meaning how many visitors does it take to get one full piece of data? Because the site is only as good as it converts. So with Boomtown, it's about 10% conversion.

intel.text: The leak is quantified in his own numbers, not ours: ~$1,500/day on PPC, ~2 sales per 100 leads, ~$1,100 customer acquisition cost, and 85% of revenue depending on the one channel he says Google is closing. That is the whole leaky-bucket argument stated by the buyer.
intel.excerpt: Spending ~$1,500/day on PPC; agents are toggled on/off for lead days based on region — PPC conversion: ~2 sales per 100 leads; customer acquisition cost ~$1,100 per sale — Main site is gulfcoastregroup.com, generating ~85% of revenue

intel.text: He named the gap we close and admitted he cannot close it himself — he does not know how to present organic to 60 agents. Attribution reporting for organic is a deliverable, not a favour, and it is the one he will feel every week.
intel.excerpt: I know it's just like hard to quantify organic for 60 agents. You know what I mean? Like, how do I, I don't know how to present that to them. Like, yes, you're going to get way less leads, but they're better quality.

intel.text: He is already sold on the thesis — 'I just feel like we have in our grasp institutional grade software that always kept companies ahead of us.' The work is not convincing him AI matters; it is being the one who ships it before his October window.
intel.excerpt: I just feel like we have in our grasp institutional grade software that always kept companies ahead of us. 100%. Now it's in our hands. It's awesome.

intel.text: The SEO teardown was run live, on his own site, before any paperwork — meta tags over 160 characters, missing alt text, broken links and a schema problem he cannot fix because the CMS is a hard-coded template. That is the PVP motion working, and the template constraint is precisely what a site we build removes.

intel.text: He is paying an Upwork team on milestones for the internal app and calls it his first dev adventure. Four products, one first-time dev relationship and a hard October date is a delivery-capacity problem we are built for.
